title: Advertisers Push Back on Disney Seeking $10 Million for 30-Second Super Bowl Commercial

facts.fact: According to a Variety report cited by WDW News Today, Disney made an initial ask of $10 million for a single 30-second commercial slot during Super Bowl LXI in 2027.
facts.quote: Disney has started their initial ask for $10 million for a single 30-second commercial slot.

facts.fact: The article states that Super Bowl ads sold for around $5 million in 2016.
facts.quote: For reference, Super Bowl ads sold for around $5 million in 2016.

facts.fact: NBC's Super Bowl LX top sales executive Mark Marshall said NBC sold a handful of commercial slots for over $10 million.
facts.quote: 2026 Super Bowl LX top sales executive Mark Marshall revealed that NBC sold a handful of commercial slots for over $10 million.

facts.fact: For Super Bowl LX, the initial starting price for commercial slots was $7 million, according to the article.

facts.fact: The article reports that the bulk of Super Bowl LX commercial slots sold between $7 million and $8 million.
facts.quote: The bulk of commercial slots were actually sold between $7 million and $8 million.

facts.fact: The article states that broadcasters such as NBC and Fox have typically sold 40% to 60% of their ad schedule before the sale season begins in May.

facts.fact: Disney claims it has 'more requests than inventory to sell' for Super Bowl LXI ad slots, a statement the article notes is not the same as orders.

facts.fact: The article states that Disney has not made progress selling its Super Bowl LXI ad inventory comparable to NBC and Fox's pre-May sales.
